title: Telemetry Slimdown — launch decision record for Console insight panels and cost surfaces
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Decision record capturing scope reductions and acceptance criteria for the initial Console public launch. Focus areas: a minimal set of insight panels (latency, error rate), a compact trace surface (sampled spans + link to full trace), and a simplified route-level cost breakdown. The goal is to ship a predictable, reviewable surface that meets reliability and onboarding needs while deferring lower-value features to subsequent releases.
background: Multiple PM/Design/Eng reviews in Feb highlighted that the original observability scope exceeded available engineering bandwidth for the launch window and increased product complexity. Customer probes showed the top needs are: (1) quick per-route latency and error visibility, (2) ability to see high-level cost contributors per route, and (3) basic trace-to-request linkages for high-severity incidents. We must reduce surface area but preserve core signals for SLO and cost debugging.
decision_summary: Trim to three insight panels (Route Vitals, Cost Overview, Recent Errors), replace a full trace viewer with a lightweight trace inspector (first/last span summary, sampled trace link), and deliver a per-route cost breakdown with top-3 cost contributors. Defer: heatmaps, full-fidelity trace flamegraphs, export CSV, and multi-route cost attribution until post-launch. This cut reduces integration work with tracing backends and lowers retention/ingest needs for initial telemetry retention.
acceptance_criteria: Route Vitals panel exists per-route showing p50/p95 latency and error rate for selected 24h window
Cost Overview shows daily cost trend for the selected route and a top-3 contributor list (model, sequence length bucket, cached vs uncached tokens)
Recent Errors panel surfaces five most-frequent error signatures with first/last occurrence timestamps and a link to the request inspector
Trace Inspector returns sampled trace metadata and links to the full trace in tracing UI when available; does not attempt to render a full flamegraph at launch
All panels load within 1.5s on a standard 90th percentile request and respect tenant-level RBAC
Telemetry queries adhere to reduced retention budget to keep storage/ingest within committed Dedicated capacity for launch
Dashboard routes have basic annotations for rollouts and can be toggled off via feature gate for early enterprise customers
tradeoffs: Pro: Faster time-to-launch and reduced infra cost by limiting retention and heavy trace renders
Con: Some power users will miss full traces and export capabilities; we accept deferred depth for earlier availability
Pro: Reduced dependencies on tracing backend feature parity simplifies QA across Dedicated/Private deployments
Con: Additional product debt to reintroduce advanced visualizations later with migration paths
implementation_notes: Use existing route metrics endpoints; add a compact aggregation query for p50/p95 to avoid new indexing work
Cost contributors computed from sampled billing tags already emitted by serving runtime; prioritize model and sequence-length buckets

Trace Inspector will fetch a small metadata payload (trace id, sample rate, span count, first/last span) and provide deep link to tracing UI (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TRACE/trace-gating-and-links)
Add feature gate `insights_v1_compact` for controlled rollout and enterprise opt-out
Avoid new export endpoints; use existing logs ingestion pipeline for any future CSV/ETL work
rollout_plan: Canary in staging with internal teams (2 days) — verify latency, RBAC, and feature gating
Gradual rollout to 10% of production orgs (1 week) — monitor error rate and query cost via infra dashboard
Expand to 100% public launch if SLOs hold for two full business days
Post-launch: collect top 5 user requests for reintroducing deferred features and prioritize next-cycle work
open_questions: What exact tenant-level retention cap should we set for launch to balance cost and debugging needs? Engineering proposed 7 days, Support prefers 14 days.
Should the Cost Overview surface absolute dollar amounts or only normalized cost units for public docs? Legal review requested for dollar display.
Do we need an explicit migration path for customers who relied on heatmaps to use the compact panels?
